gloss: reduced service (of trains/buses); thinning out scheduled runs

definitions.gloss: reduced service; thinning out scheduled runs (trains, buses)
definitions.explanation: The practice of operating fewer trains or buses than usual on a given line, either due to disruption (bad weather, accidents, equipment trouble) or due to planned reductions in service (lower demand, staff shortages).

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}のため{間引|まび}き{運転|うんてん}を{実施|じっし}している。
examples.english: We are operating reduced service because of the typhoon.

examples.japanese: {電車|でんしゃ}が{間引|まび}き{運転|うんてん}になっているので{注意|ちゅうい}してください。
examples.english: Please note that the trains are running on a reduced schedule.

examples.japanese: {大雪|おおゆき}の{影響|えいきょう}で、{朝|あさ}の{通勤|つうきん}{時間帯|じかんたい}に{間引|まび}き{運転|うんてん}が{行|おこな}われた。
examples.english: Due to the heavy snow, reduced service was in effect during the morning commute.

examples.japanese: {運転士|うんてんし}{不足|ぶそく}のため、{一部|いちぶ}の{路線|ろせん}で{間引|まび}き{運転|うんてん}が{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: Due to a shortage of drivers, reduced service continues on some lines.

notes:
Composed of {間引|まび}き (thinning out) + {運転|うんてん} (operation, running). The verb {間引|まび}く originally refers to thinning out seedlings in a garden — removing some so that the rest have room to grow — and is used metaphorically to describe removing scheduled runs from a transit timetable.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {間引|まび}き{運転|うんてん}を{実施|じっし}する: to implement reduced service
- {間引|まび}き{運転|うんてん}を{行|おこな}う: to operate on a reduced schedule
- {間引|まび}き{運転|うんてん}になる: to go on a reduced schedule
- {間引|まび}き{運転|うんてん}が{続|つづ}く: reduced service continues
- {一部|いちぶ}{区間|くかん}で{間引|まび}き{運転|うんてん}: reduced service on a partial section of the line

RELATED WORDS:
- {運休|うんきゅう}: service suspension — more extreme; no runs at all
- {遅延|ちえん}: delay — trains still run but behind schedule
- {折返|おりかえ}し{運転|うんてん}: shuttle operation — trains turn back partway due to a blocked section
- {徐行|じょこう}{運転|うんてん}: slow operation — trains run at reduced speed
- {平常|へいじょう}{運転|うんてん}: normal operation — the baseline

USAGE:
{間引|まび}き{運転|うんてん} is one of several standard railway terms heard in Japanese station announcements and news reports during service disruptions. Passengers expect longer waits between trains on the affected line.
